items.title: [Bug] gpt-oss model doesn't support multiple system message input
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

When using the gpt-oss model, the model processes only the first system message. If two system messages are provided in the messages array, the second one is silently ignored. This differs from the behavior of other models, which usually merge or respect multiple system messages.

### Reproduction

command to start the server
```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model /home/ubuntu/models/openai/gpt-oss-20b --port=8080 --tp-size=2 --context-length=3000 --mem-fraction-static=0.8 --reasoning-parser=gpt-oss
```

payload 
```
curl http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-oss",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "system",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "text",
            "text": "You are a helpful knowledge bot"
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "role": "system",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "text",
            "text": "you know my name is Bob"
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "text",
            "text": "What is my name?"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```
response
```

Then user asks \"What is my name?\" The user hasn't given any name previously. So we cannot know. According to policy, must not provide false info, must ask for clarification. We can respond with \"I don't know your name. Could you let me know?\" That's likely. No policy violation.\n\nWe should keep a friendly tone.",

```
while if I put the system messages in one it works

items.title: [Bug] Llama4 fails to run on Python 3.9 (AssertionError)
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Running llama 4 with Python 3.9 get AssertionError

e.g.`python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct --tp 8 --context-length 65536`

The error does not occur in python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12.

### Reproduction

#### Python 3.9 (AssertionError)

```bash
mkdir 3-9-test
cd 3-9-test
uv init --python 3.9
uv add "sglang[all]>=0.4.6.post3" setuptools
export HF_TOKEN=<token>
uv run -m sglang.launch_server --model-path meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct --tp 8 --context-length 65536 --log-level debug

# Boom!! AssertionError!!
```

[Error log in python 3.9](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20160697/python-3-9.log)


#### Python 3.10, and etc (This is OK)

```bash
mkdir 3-10-test
cd 3-10-test
uv init --python 3.10
uv add "sglang[all]>=0.4.6.post3" setuptools
export HF_TOKEN=<token>
uv run -m sglang.launch_server --model-path meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct --tp 8 --context-length 65536 --log-level debug

# Runs OK
```

items.title: [Feature] P100/Cuda 6.1 support
items.body:
### Motivation

As per https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/1059 , P100/pascal/6.1 support is not currently a target. This feature request is an official request to support it. This GPU is the least expensive hardware that will run modern LLMs, and is a common GPU in both academia and common use.

This issue was created as the original was locked with the cryptic phrase, "It makes nonsense for me.", the meaning of which was not clear in context. This issue is intended to be a place where the community can discuss support for these GPUs, as well as petition for support.

### Related resources

_No response_
